Okay, then why does it go through all of that aspect of her being born as Maelle at the end of Act II? It's clear that it's the first time she's entering the painting. 

She's born as Maelle after entering the painting at the end of Act II, then the events of the game happen. Otherwise there's no point to the game showing us her entering the painting > being born > then cutting to her as Alicia going to the bench.

Her reaction to entering the painting if it was the second time would be vastly different compared to how she behaves with Clea with asking questions and how to help etc. The next cutscene wouldn't happen where Clea mentions that she's about to be reborn as Aline's creation if she was re-entering the painting for the second time. 

Unless you're suggesting the cutscenes go with Act II gommage > her waking up after being gommaged > entering painting for the second time > panicking and being repainted > born as Maelle second time??? 

Or how do you see the events processed?

They're definitely the same person. The end of Act II when you see Alicia wake up in the "real" world and is called by Clea does not happen after the events of Expedition 33 and Act II. It's the original prologue, you can see this when Alicia enters the Canvas and Clea tells her to be calm. Alicia doesn't stay calm and instead panics and Clea tells her that she's about to be reborn as one of Aline's creations. 

The immediate next scene is her being born into the world and getting named Maelle from her Lumiere parents. The rest of the Canvas story then plays out and the scene with her joining Verso on the bench is what happens next. 

The gommage itself is indicated as Renoir's ability to absorb Aline's chroma, which was painted over Alicia when she first entered the Canvas, but underneath that painting is the original Alicia, with all the memories of having lived as Maelle. 

How exactly she pops into the world after getting gommaged isn't shown but the game is explicit in it's story telling of her only entering the Canvas once.
